title: A password signs a device in to jellyscale's own API
description: Serves "Joining and signing in are easy and safe.".
acceptanceCriteria: A right name and password signs a device in. An account holds one sign-in per installation: signing in again from the same installation replaces the first, whose token is then refused. After sign-out the next request with that token is 401 on every route of every replica, the device stays known to the guessing bounds for 30 days, and the account's other devices keep working.

A wrong password, an unknown name, an account with no password and a disabled account given a wrong password get the identical 401 `credentials-not-accepted`, in the same time: the same password work for each. Today's bounds apply (20 wrong passwords per name, 10 per known device, 10 per network address, each per 15 minutes), shared with Jellyfin's sign-in, and a name that does not exist counts exactly as an account does. No answer, refusal or timing tells a viewer which names exist.

Every refusal carries a reason and the `action` Octave explains it with. A bounded try gets 429 `too-many-tries` with `retryAfterSeconds` (1 to 900) and `scope` (`name`, `device` or `network`), and no password is checked. 403 `account-off` comes only for a disabled account given its right password. An account disabled, deleted or given a new password while a sign-in runs gets 401 or 403, never success and never a server error. A malformed body is 400 `invalid-body`.
Every capability it adds is in the published contract (JS-183): sign-in, sign-out, `/me` and the `sign-in` capability, each passing the contract's conformance check.

The sign-in answer and `/me` agree on the account, the profile and the device, each with its own id, stable across new tokens and upgrades. The device id is the server's, never the token or the installation id.

No stored value admits a request. After signing in through both APIs and redeeming a TV code, every value read from every database table is tried as a token and as a TV-code secret, and all are refused; a stored hash presented as a token is refused. A TV that asks again for its approved code's sign-in gets the same one. Tokens issued before this release are hashed by JS-227 (D-20261127-token-hashing-upgrade).

`GET /me` answers the caller's account, profile and device. It is 401 `unauthorized` through either of two real api processes after sign-out through either API, replacement by a new sign-in, a password change or reset, or the account being disabled or deleted.
A token is accepted as `Authorization: Bearer`, as well as in today's spellings, on every route that takes a token, media included.

`account-off` is served from the account's disabled state as it is set today, and enabling the account again lets the right password sign in. The setting in configuration comes with JS-194 (D-20261127-account-disable-configuration).

Until the cutover, a token it gives is accepted wherever a Jellyfin sign-in's token is, media and the outage grace of invariant 37 included. Jellyfin's session and device lists show a device signed in through the new API by the server's device id, never its installation id; devices signed in through Jellyfin's routes show what they show today.
Sign-in, sign-out and `/me` are `preview` once served, and the server lists the `sign-in` capability.
notes: Amended 2026-11-27 by D-20261127-sign-in-first, decided by the product owner: dependsOn JS-223 (replacing JS-216), and criteria 7 to 11 added. Condition: the lead has not shown that accepting the token on Jellyfin's routes is cheap. If it costs more than the sign-in itself, the lead brings a brief before building it. Without it, Octave can test sign-in but not continue into the app with that token. Criteria refined 2026-11-27 by D-20261127-js184-criteria, decided by the product owner. Tokens are hashed by D-20261127-token-hashing-upgrade (pre-upgrade tokens by JS-227). TV-code tokens are encrypted under the secret by D-20261127-tv-code-token-sealed. DOMAINS invariants 26 and 65 are reworded in this task's change, citing them. docs/running.md carries the upgrade note: "Tokens issued before this release are stored as they were until the next release hashes them. During this rollout, a device that signs in on a new replica may be refused by an older one until every replica is replaced, and signs in again." If accepting the token on Jellyfin's routes proves dearer than sign-in itself, brief the product owner.
